html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CLI: command-line interface; A2A: agent to agent; OAuth: open authorization; PKCE: Proof Key for Code Exchange; RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; LLM: large language model; HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act; FedRAMP: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program; GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; BAA: business associate agreement; DPA: data processing addendum; ADR: architecture decision record; BM25: Best Matching 25, a keyword ranking function; ZDR: zero data retention

  • One-page decision tables for each domain
  • The names, numbers and limits worth memorizing
  • The distractor patterns that make wrong answers attractive

2Decision Chooser

D1 Solution Design (17%) and D2 Models, Prompting, Context (13%)

Decision Deciding question Answer
Pattern Are the steps known? Known: workflow; unpredictable: orchestrator-workers or agent; start simplest
Multi-agent? High value, parallel, beyond one context? Yes: orchestrator-worker; else workflow
Model tier What is the binding constraint? Volume and latency: light; balanced: mid; hard reasoning: strong; prove with evals
Prompt content Does it repeat? Static first, dynamic last, cache the prefix
Technique Format or tone hard to describe? Few-shot; multi-step reasoning: chain-of-thought or effort
Context too big What is bloating it? Prune, compact, isolate, external memory
Prompt reuse Procedure or background? Skill (procedure) · Project or knowledge (background) · MCP (live data)

D3 Integration (19%)

Decision Deciding question Answer
Too many tools Does the role need them? Remove unneeded; then defer with tool search; code execution for data-heavy tools
Security gap Who is acting and what may they do? Per-user identity and authorization in code; least privilege; secrets server-side
Integration Reusable shared capability? MCP; simple owned call: API/CLI; delegate to another agent: A2A
MCP auth HTTP or STDIO? HTTP: OAuth 2.1, PKCE, audience check, no passthrough; STDIO: environment
RAG or not Corpus size and change? Under about 200,000 tokens: cached prompt; larger or filtered: RAG
Retrieval Data shape? Prose: hybrid plus rerank · identifiers: keyword · tables: SQL · code: search tools
Wrong answers after refresh Where first? Retrieval and indexing
Latency vs accuracy Client priority? Measure; stream, cache, route, batch; justify
Observability Scale and privacy? Metrics for all, sampled redacted traces, quality sampling, cost attribution

D4 Evaluation (16%), D5 Governance (14%), D6 Stakeholders (14%), D7 Productivity (7%)

Decision Answer
Define quality Numeric criteria on a held-out dataset, several dimensions
Grading Code (checkable) · LLM judge with rubric, different model, calibrated · human for calibration
Release a change Offline eval, then A/B or canary, baseline comparison, rollback
Diagnose Reproduce; find the layer; inspect what the model saw; one change
Optimize Cost per successful task; reject savings that break gated metrics
Guardrails Layers; assume the model can be wrong; hard controls in code; approvals for irreversible actions
Injection Untrusted content as data; no instructions in tool results; screen outputs; red-team
Human oversight Gate before irreversible; sample after reversible; queue by risk; meaningful review
HIPAA / FedRAMP / GDPR BAA and eligible features / authorized route (GovCloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads) / DPA, minimization, residency
Ethics Subgroup tests, human decisions, disclosure, citations
Discovery All stakeholders, real examples, measurable outcomes, constraints
SLA Honest, measurable; quality as percent on a test set; fallbacks
Handoff Versioned prompts, evals, runbooks, ADRs, owners
Team policy Managed settings; commit CLAUDE.md and shared settings; hooks and permissions deterministic
Exam tip

When two options both work, prefer the one that is simple, least-privileged, measured, cost-aware and compliant.

3Names and Values to Know

Item Value
Exam CCAR-P; 63 items; 120 min; 720 of 1,000; USD 175; valid 12 months
Domain weights D3 19 · D1 17 · D4 16 · D5 14 · D6 14 · D2 13 · D7 7
Tiers Haiku fast and cheap · Sonnet balanced · Opus strong · Fable strongest
Context / output 1M tokens / 128K
Savings Batch 50% off; cache reads 10% of base input (5% / 2.5% on some tiers)
Cache Static first; up to 4 breakpoints; 5 min or 1 hour; about 512-token minimum
Agents vs chat tokens Agents about 4x; multi-agent about 15x
Tool search Use at 10+ tools or over 10k tokens; accuracy falls beyond 30 to 50 tools; keep 3 to 5 loaded
Contextual retrieval 50 to 100 token context; failure -35%, -49%, -67% with BM25 and rerank; rerank 150 to 20
No-RAG threshold About 200,000 tokens
Eval start About 20 cases
MCP auth OAuth 2.1 for HTTP; 401 token, 403 insufficient scope
ZDR No storage at rest; per org; no browser calls
HIPAA BAA plus eligible features
FedRAMP Via GovCloud or Vertex with Assured Workloads; not the direct API
Covered Models 30-day retention
Claude Code scopes Managed > command line > project local > shared project > user

[Verify live] Model names, prices, platform authorizations and settings keys change; the principles behind them are what the questions test.

Exam tip

Numbers matter most where they decide a design choice: about 55k tokens of tool definitions, 30 to 50 tools, 200,000 tokens for the no-RAG threshold, 15x tokens for multi-agent.

4Distractor Patterns

Pattern Why it is tempting Why it fails
Add logging or a confirmation instead of removing a tool Feels safe Compensating, not least privilege
A bigger model fixes it Capability sounds like the cure Does not fix retrieval, authorization or design
Always the largest / always the smallest Simple rule Ignores the eval
An agent for a fixed task Modern More cost and compounding errors
Truncate or shrink blindly Cheap Loses needed content or quality
Put everything in a vector store One tool Wrong for tables, identifiers, code
Blame the model after a data refresh Easy target Check retrieval and indexing first
Stronger prompt wording Quick Not enforceable
Shared credential for convenience Simple No per-user permissions
Judge by a few examples Fast Needs datasets and controlled tests
Promise 100 percent accuracy Wins the deal Quality is statistical
Assume any route is compliant Convenient Contract, features and platform matter
Log everything with full content Debuggable Cost and privacy risk
Skip handoff docs Time pressure System cannot be operated
Exam tip

A distractor often adds a control after the fact (logging, a confirmation, a bigger model); the correct answer removes the cause.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Design Simplest pattern; workflows for known steps; multi-agent only when it pays
Models Smallest that passes evals; route; pin
Context Cache static prefix; prune, compact, isolate
Integration Remove, then defer tools; identity in code; MCP vs API vs A2A; retrieval by data shape
Evaluation Numeric criteria, datasets, mixed grading, A/B, diagnose by layer
Governance Layered guardrails, human gates, right compliance route, ethics tests
Stakeholders Discovery, honest trade-offs, SLAs, documentation, lifecycle
Teams Managed settings, shared CLAUDE.md, hooks, telemetry
